newsitem.title: USA: US late spot prods soar with NYMEX, APIs help heat.
newsitem.headline: US late spot prods soar with NYMEX, APIs help heat.

text.p: U.S. late spot gasoline and heating oil surged 2.50 cents higher tracking futures by late Tuesday, players said, with heating oil getting an extra boost from API data showing continuing poor distillate stock builds.

The API report showed primary distillate stocks rising a skimpy 303,000 barrels for the week ending Sept. 20, far short of the one-to-three-million-barrel weekly builds common during the weeks leading up to the winter heating season.
Among the distillates, U.S. heating oil stocks grew by 1.52 million barrels, offset by a drop of 1.22 million barrels of low sulfur diesel.
October heating oil jumped about 0.40 cents a gallon in after-hours ACCESS trade following release of the API report, adding to a sharp 2.20-cent futures gain scored earlier in the day.

Heating oil differentials, however, held steady througuout the day and early evening, traders said, with offers at about 0.20 cent below the screen in New York Harbor and 2.60 cents below in the Gulf Coast.
"Distillates overall didn't build much, but heat grew enough that people might worry a little less about the ability to build stocks" in time for winter, one Gulf trader said.
